newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile judge quizzes Davila over hospital scanner.
newsitem.headline: Chile judge quizzes Davila over hospital scanner.

text.p: A Chilean judge questioned former Codelco futures dealer Juan Pablo Davila over his claims that Codelco advisers asked him to use profits from futures deals to buy equipment for a military hospital.
Judge Jose Benquis quizzed Davila for three hours in a face-to-face hearing with former Codelco CEO Patricio Contesse who headed the state copper giant at the time of the purchase in the late 1980s.
The hearings were one of the last stages in a three-year long probe by Benquis into failed futures deals by Davila which cost Codelco $175 million in 1993.
Contesse, who left the corporation in 1990, has denied that Codelco was involved in buying the scanner for the hospital.
"I repeated the (same) declarations as I have made over the last year," said Contesse after the hearing.
Davila has said that an adviser to Codelco, Col Mario Piraino, asked him to use funds from futures operations to buy the scanner.
Davila, who was fired when the losses were uncovered in 1994, faces charges of fraud and carrying out business "incompatible" with his position.
Benquis has said he hopes to wrap up his probe by the end of the month.
